title: Reading a malformed mmseqs database can panic
body:
`PrefilterDb` and the db writers in nail/src/mmseqs.rs read files mmseqs wrote, and several reads use `expect`, `unwrap` or unchecked indexing. The input survey on nail-d551f7 found these by reading the code; it triggered none of them:

- `PrefilterDb::from_path`: `.expect("failed to parse index line")` on each `.index` field, unchecked `tokens[1]` and `tokens[2]`, `tokens[2] - 1` underflowing for a record of length 0, and `.expect("bad DB split suffix")`
- `PrefilterDb::get`: `prefix_sum[file_idx]` and `descriptors[prf_idx]`, which panic when the prefilter db holds fewer records than there are queries
- the db writers: `db_path.file_name().unwrap().to_str().unwrap()`, on a tmp path that is not UTF-8 or ends in `..`
- the profile db writer: the consensus residue lookup `.get(..).unwrap()`
- nail/src/util.rs: the one-byte read helper, with `seek(..).expect` and `read_exact(..).expect`

Each needs a db mmseqs wrote badly, or an odd tmp path.

## Proposal

Return an error naming the db path and the record in place of each `expect` and `unwrap`.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/69ba1bc3
notes.text: Only PrefilterDb::from_path was hardened, per Jack. The other sites in the body are invariants nail itself holds (prefix_sum and descriptors indexed by query, the consensus residue table) or paths nobody takes (a --tmp-dir ending in .. or not utf-8, an io error inside the one-byte read helper), and a panic stays the outcome there.
